name: Hydrogen storage in salt caverns
applications: buffer between electrolysers and steady users
principle: Caverns are dissolved in deep salt formations by solution mining, then filled with compressed hydrogen. Salt is nearly impermeable to hydrogen and creeps to seal fractures, so caverns can be cycled many times. A cushion gas stays in the cavern to keep the walls stable, and withdrawn gas is dried before use.

process_steps.name: Delivery to users
equipment: pipeline to power plant or industry

performance.metric: storage capacity, two caverns (ACES Delta phase one)
performance.basis: two solution-mined caverns about 220 ft wide and 1,200 ft tall, tops 3,500 to 4,100 ft deep

reference_plants.name: ACES Delta, Utah
reference_plants.capacity: 220 MW electrolysis, up to 100 t/day hydrogen, 300 GWh in two caverns, feeding the 840 MW Intermountain Power combined cycle
reference_plants.status: USD 504.4 million conditional DOE loan guarantee, April 2022
